Representation level: L1 (proxy). CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline (native inspect-revise protocol). This is not a Blender protocol-equivalent result.

Observed in the 24 reference samples (0.00-5.28 s, 25 fps, 133 frames): one continuous shot with no cuts. A red Hong Kong taxi (red body, light roof, roof sign) drives away from the camera along a multi-lane one-way street at night. It is first framed tightly from behind and above with an extreme telephoto lens. It overtakes a silver car (about 0.4-0.7 s) and passes parked cars on the right kerb, under overhanging shop signs, with a white minibus ahead. From about 2.1 s the camera zooms out quickly and tilts up. The taxi becomes tiny and the street canyon with neon signs, then the high-rise skyline with mountains, comes into view. From about 3.0 s to the end the zoom-out slows and the camera pans right, revealing trees and a flyover with queued trucks in the lower right.

Reconstruction:
- Geometry: box/cylinder/sphere proxies only. The street has lane dashes, yellow stripe bands and pavements. Cars are body, glass-cabin and roof boxes with tail lights, plate and wheels. The taxi has a roof light. Trucks are cab plus cargo box. There are flat-coloured emissive hanging signs, a tall pink/white vertical neon, and building boxes along both sides of the street plus seeded procedural mid and far city blocks. Landmark far towers include a gold-crowned tower and a dome. Mountains are cones and the sky is a gradient dome. There are also tree spheres and an elevated flyover deck with pillars and barriers.
- Motion: the taxi follows an analytical distance profile (95 m/s scene units until 1.6 s, then easing to 35 m/s, reflecting the time-lapse look) with a small early lane drift and rolling wheels. Other traffic uses constant or eased analytical profiles. Flyover trucks creep slowly and near-lane vehicles move faster. All of it is absolute-time and deterministic.
- Camera: a static elevated camera at (14, 40, 0). Focal length is key-framed per sample. From 0 to 2.08 s it is derived from the observed taxi image width and the modelled taxi distance. After that it comes from the apparent size change of the neon landmark. Orientation keeps the taxi at its observed image position up to 2.08 s, then keeps the neon landmark at its observed image position. Hermite spline interpolation runs between samples. There are no cuts.
- Inference vs observation: the world distances, camera height, street layout, sign depths and speeds are inferred from apparent sizes and offsets in the samples. The in-between motion is interpolated. Building layouts, far city, flyover traffic and colours are approximate proxies.

Render feedback: none received yet (initial generation). Remaining uncertainties: the exact lens and zoom curve, the camera height, whether the real camera also translated, the taxi's exact position after about 2.1 s when it is tiny or occluded, and the detailed building arrangement in the wide shot.
